draft.title: Charges in magnetic fields
card: A charge moving in a magnetic field feels a force F = qvB sin θ. Here q is the charge, v is its speed, B is the field strength and θ is the angle between the velocity and the field.
The force is at right angles to both the velocity and the field. A charge at rest, or one moving along the field (θ = 0°), feels no force.

The force changes the direction of the motion but not the speed, so it does no work. If the velocity is at right angles to the field, the charge moves in a circle, with the magnetic force acting as the centripetal force: qvB = mv²/r.
This gives the radius r = mv/qB. A faster or heavier particle moves in a bigger circle. A stronger field or a larger charge makes the circle smaller.
draft.remember: The magnetic force is sideways to the motion, so it turns the charge and never speeds it up.

a.q: A proton moves at right angles to a uniform magnetic field. What happens to its speed while it moves in the field?
opts: It stays constant, as the force only changes direction
It increases, as the force acts on the proton
It decreases, as the field slows moving charges
It rises on half the circle and falls on the other half
a.why: The magnetic force is at right angles to the velocity, so it does no work on the proton. Its direction changes but its speed stays constant. The force does act on the proton, but it acts sideways rather than along the motion, so it cannot speed it up.
a.clue: Think about the direction of the force compared with the direction of motion.

b.q: Two electrons enter the same uniform magnetic field at right angles to it. Electron X has twice the speed of electron Y. How do their circular paths compare?
opts: X's circle has twice the radius of Y's
X's circle has half the radius of Y's
X's circle has four times the radius of Y's
Both circles have the same radius
b.why: Since r = mv/qB, and m, q and B are the same for both electrons, the radius is proportional to speed. X moves twice as fast, so its radius is twice as big. The radius does not stay the same, because a faster charge needs a larger circle to be turned by the same force.
b.clue: Use r = mv/qB and see which quantities are the same for both electrons.

a.best: It stays constant, as the force only changes direction

b.best: X's circle has twice the radius of Y's

problems.detail: The why says a faster charge needs a larger circle 'to be turned by the same force', but the force is not the same. F = qvB, so electron X, moving twice as fast, feels twice the force of Y. The radius doubles because mv²/r must equal qvB, not because the force is equal.

check.summary: The card, the remember line and both questions are correct. The why for (b) wrongly says both electrons feel the same force, when X feels twice the force because F = qvB.
